switchingHighlights: 42% of Corona loyalists redirected to Heineken when Corona was OOS — the single largest inter-brand switching flow in the entire matrix.
46% of Heineken loyalists redirected to Corona when Heineken was OOS — the two brands are near-perfect mutual substitutes.
65% of Heineken replacement-choice buyers came from Corona (26 people) or Rescue Club (6 people) — the #1 and #2 most popular first-choice brands.
Clausthaler was the biggest proportional net gainer (+27), driven by Rescue Club IPA loyalists who treated it as their craft substitute.
Rescue Club IPA lost the most replacement share (−28), consistent with its highly category-specific appeal — IPA enthusiasts forced into lager territory dispersed widely.
When first-choice brands were mother brands, 58.8% of replacement choices stayed within the mother-brand category — above chance.
switchingMatrixDescription: The 6×6 inter-brand switching matrix revealed a clear competitive structure. Rows represent the original first-choice brand; columns show the replacement selected. The dominant Heineken ↔ Corona inter-brand flow is the single most prominent feature: when Corona is forced OOS, 42% of its loyalists redirect to Heineken — by far the largest single inter-brand flow.
